caption: Two halves take turns: one half's piston pushes the other half a block forward, then that half's piston pulls the first half after it; an observer on each half sees the move and fires the next piston, so the machine crawls one block every 10 ticks. Detail: the smallest flying machine (6 blocks; nothing with 5 flies), each half an observer, a slime block and a sticky piston; all slime; also 39 other layouts (observers looking other ways) in tracks/fly/layouts

Flies straight down, one block every 10 ticks, with only observers firing the pistons; it works only when built facing east or west (facing north or south it shakes in place, because of the order the game updates blocks in). Detail: 6 blocks, one honey and one slime; also 3 other layouts in tracks/fly/layouts

The same two-halves-taking-turns machine as the slime one, but one half is glued with honey: honey and slime do not stick to each other, so the halves touch without gluing together. Detail: 6 blocks, 10 ticks per block; also 6 other slime + honey layouts in tracks/fly/layouts

The 6-block flying machine carrying 9 extra blocks on its front half, the most one half can drag along (a piston moves at most 12 blocks). Detail: 8 slime and a gold block in a column up from the front slime; 15 blocks in all, still one block every 10 ticks

The 6-block flying machine carrying 18 extra blocks, 9 on each half: the biggest load it can move (one more block and the pull fails). Detail: 8 slime and a gold block up from the front slime, the same down from the rear slime; 24 blocks in all

A flying machine that carries cargo: the 6-block machine with a column of extra blocks stuck to its front half; every block rides along at the same speed, up to 9 on each half. Detail: the family carries n = 1 to 18 blocks in 6 + n blocks (a piston moves at most 12 blocks: the 3-block half plus 9); this card carries 1 block

The fastest sideways flying machine, one block every 9 ticks: it works like the 6-block one, but a redstone block riding on the front half switches the rear piston on the instant it lands instead of waiting for an observer. Detail: 7 blocks (the 6-block engine without its rear observer, plus a second slime carrying the redstone block); the pulled piston fires 1 tick after landing instead of 2

Flies straight up, one block every 9 ticks, like the slime one but with a honey half (honey and slime do not stick to each other, so the halves can touch). Detail: 6 blocks; a redstone block on the honey half fires the pusher as it lands; also 3 other layouts in tracks/fly/layouts

A flying machine that pulls a train of wagons: every wagon has its own piston that pulls the next wagon after it, so the train can be any length and still moves one block every 10 ticks. Detail: 5 + 3n blocks for n wagons (judged up to 16); a sticky piston on the rear slime pulls wagon 1 each cycle

Flies straight down, one block every 10 ticks, whichever way it faces: the two halves take turns pulling each other down, and a redstone block riding on one half fires the other piston the moment it lands. Detail: 6 blocks, all slime; the observer-only down flyers work only facing east or west; also 18 other layouts in tracks/fly/layouts

Flies straight down, one block every 10 ticks, whichever way it faces, glued with honey instead of slime. Detail: 6 blocks; a redstone block riding on one half fires the other piston as it lands; also 1 other layout in tracks/fly/layouts

Flies straight up, one block every 9 ticks: one piston pushes the top half up, the observer on the top half then fires its piston to pull the bottom half after it, and a redstone block on the bottom half fires the first piston again the moment it arrives. Detail: 6 blocks, all slime; the redstone block takes the place of the rear observer and saves a tick

Flying machine with docking stations, 15 blocks, and an on/off lever: a 6-block flying machine (two sticky pistons, two slime blocks, two observers) shuttles between two docking stations, 98 ticks per round trip. Each station has an obsidian wall that stops the machine and an observer that sees it arrive and fires, 2 ticks later, into a dust behind the leading piston, which pushes the machine back the other way. At the station with the lever, the observer stands on a sticky piston: lever off pulls it aside, so the machine docks there and stays; lever on pushes it back into place, and a moved observer fires, so the docked machine leaves at once and shuttles again.
